BCDRPC Agency Comments
May 5, 1972
Endangered Species Conservation Act of 1972
Borkeley-Charleston-Dorchester Regional Planning Council
We concur with the statements in the summary and emphasize that they be endorsed in their most stringent form. The protection of endangered or potentially endangered species should not be jeapordized by the initigating measures of by the proposed alternatives, either of which would weaken the effectiveness of the proposed legislation.
Furthermore, any individual whose economic pursuits are impeded by the acitivities of an endangered species should not be licensed in any way control this activity without first having his case reviewed by the Federal Agencies involved in the proposed legislation. If the case for management is considered valid, then these federal agencies should monitor the proposed legislation.
Preservation of habitat should be a primary concern in the conservation of endangered species and any confrontation between commercial interests and habitat preservation, eq. mature cypress forest versus lumber interests, should be subject to Federal review.
